messages.content:
Risk: Legal accountability issues
Description: Determining who is responsible for an AI model is challenging without good documentation and governance processes. The use of synthetic data in model development adds further complexity, since the lack of standardized frameworks for recording synthetic data design choices and verification steps makes accountability harder to establish.
Concern: 'If ownership for development of the model is uncertain, it may not be clear who would be liable and responsible for the problems with it or can answer questions about it. Users of models without clear ownership might find challenges with compliance with regulations.'
Policy: Governance and Compliance

Candidate ontology classes:
- http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/OAE_0001337: evidence of biological plausity of adverse event causality — an adverse event causality evidence that has an outcome of biological plausity. [found by 4/12 queries]
  Siblings: adverse event causality evidence from case report, adverse event causality evidence from combined sources, adverse event causality evidence from controlled observational study
- http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/OAE_0000128: causality of adverse event — None [found by 4/12 queries]
  Siblings: severity of adverse event, physical quality of a process, increased process quality
- https://www.omg.org/spec/Commons/RegulatoryAgencies/RegulatoryReport: regulatory report — document required to support operational transparency that demonstrates compliance with some specification, law, policy, restriction, or other rule specified by a regulatory agency [found by 8/12 queries]
  Siblings: technical specification document, registry, transaction record
- https://www.omg.org/spec/Commons/BusinessAuthorizations/Authorization: authorisation — situation in which a party authorizes someone to act on their behalf or to have specific capabilities under certain conditions for some period of time [found by 8/12 queries]
  Siblings: trade, ownership control situation, study
- http://taxonomy-refiner.io/ontologies/cso#DangerousInformation: Dangerous Information — Knowledge or instructions that enable serious physical harm, weapons production, or dangerous activities when acquired or executed by untrained individuals outside regulated contexts. [found by 7/12 queries]
  Siblings: Sexual Content, Intellectual Property, Hate and Discrimination
- https://www.omg.org/spec/Commons/BusinessAuthorizations/AuthorizingParty: authorising party — party that delegates some role, authority, or control to another party [from restriction: hasAuthorizingParty on Authorization]
  Siblings: owner, registrar, controlling party
- https://www.omg.org/spec/Commons/BusinessAuthorizations/AuthorizedParty: authorised party — party that has been given the ability to act on behalf of another party or to have specified capabilities under some set of guidelines for some period of time [from restriction: hasAuthorizedParty on Authorization]
  Siblings: Occupation Role, Contractor Role, service provider

axes.rationale: The authorising party is the entity that delegates authority, which is crucial in determining who is responsible for the AI model and its governance.
Regulatory reports are essential for demonstrating compliance and transparency, which are key concerns in establishing legal accountability for AI models.
